result.topic_en: The page ends a remark on congruence groups in one variable and then begins a proof that any finite group of linear transformations can be transformed so that its substitution coefficients are rational functions of roots of unity; the first attempted lemma is struck through.

items.english: If a finite group of transformations is given, one can always transform it so that the coefficients of the linear substitutions are rational functions of roots of unity.

items.english: (Struck through) If one has m substitutions, with f_1, f_2, ..., f_m the corresponding bilinear forms, and if one can determine parameters λ so that the characteristic equation of λ_1 f_1 + ... + λ_m f_m has all distinct roots, then the group can always be transformed into another group whose substitution coefficients are rational functions.
